Unfortunately, my experience with Blackheath Veterinary Surgery was very disappointing.

I had recently returned to the UK with my dog, who had developed a skin infection likely caused by new environmental allergens. When I booked the appointment, I was told that because she had come from overseas she would need a Brucella test costing around £220. I had no issue with this, I had already spent a significant amount ensuring all the correct import tests and paperwork were completed, and I was happy to comply with any UK requirements.

However, I explained that my dog needed to be seen urgently because of her skin condition. I was told I would only need to wait outside while the Brucella test results came back, so I paid the consultation fee and asked for a pro forma invoice for the testing. It was only at that point that it became clear the sample would actually need to be sent to a laboratory. After calling to clarify, I was informed the results would take around two weeks.

Waiting two weeks with an active skin infection wasn't an option, so I cancelled the consultation before it took place. The practice agreed that the communication around the Brucella testing should have been clearer and also agreed to refund my consultation fee.

That was over a month ago. Despite several follow-up emails and being repeatedly told that someone would get back to me, I have still not received the agreed refund.

Mistakes happen, but poor communication followed by a failure to honour an agreed refund has left me very disappointed.

I recently contacted this vet practice for assistance with a cat I was cat sitting. They were super helpful and they were able to accommodate my request even on a busy day when the vets were fully booked with consults and surgeries. The person I spoke to on the phone was very approachable, reassuring and friendly, and they made sure to follow through so that everything went smoothly. Having worked in veterinary practice as a nurse for years, I know how difficult it can be to fulfil requests on a short notice when things are busy, so I just want to say a massive thank you to the team for helping me so promptly!

I would give zero or minus, if it was possible. Unfortunate but true - that it is staff members who build or ruin the reputation of a clinic. This is why my review concerns one particular member of the staff: Dr Dominic Dalby. In October 2025 he did ultrasound for my dog and offered to put her down due to suspected bleeding of a splenic tumour. My dog is still alive and well after I sought 2nd opinion on the very next day. I am wondering if this clinic puts the dogs down based on suspicion of Dr Dalby. If that's not the case, and he was confident, then his clinical skills and knowledge are far below expected standards. Mistakes happen, but this is not some "lungs vs heart" or "chronic vs acute kidneys". Every dog owner knows how serious and life-threatening condition a bleeding splenic tumour is, and that it should be regarded as an emergency. Dr Dalby didn’t even offer to refer us to the hospital (what a reassuring arrogance) , that's how certain he must have been. Well, the 2nd opinion on the very next day confirmed no bleeding. If I trusted Dr Dalby, I would have let him to kill my precious friend. I would recommend every pet owner to avoid consultation with Dr Dalby, if you use this clinic. And/or always seek 2nd opinion. Otherwise you may lose your best friend to nothing.
